name: lalrpop
description: LR(1)/LALR(1) parser generator with .lalrpop grammar files and inline Rust actions

license.comment: Workspace Cargo.toml: `license = "Apache-2.0 OR MIT"` (dual), inherited by both `lalrpop` and `lalrpop-util`.

approach.comment: Grammar lives in a `.lalrpop` file; the `lalrpop` crate runs from `build.rs` (or the CLI) and emits a Rust module that is pulled in via `lalrpop_mod!`.

implementation.comment: Runtime crate `lalrpop-util` depends only on `regex-automata` (optional); generator crate deps (petgraph, ena, regex, string_cache, sha3, ...) are all pure Rust.

crates-io.comment: `lalrpop` is the generator (build-dependency); `lalrpop-util` is the runtime crate the user's binary links. Versions must be kept in sync.

documentation.comment: The LALRPOP Book (tutorial, lexer tutorial, cheat sheet); API reference at docs.rs/lalrpop-util.

latest-stable-version.comment: Checked 2026-09-19; published 2026-03-11. Research reflects lalrpop / lalrpop-util 0.23.x (Rust 2024 edition, `lexer` feature on by default).

grammar-class.comment: README: "uses LR(1) by default (though you can opt for LALR(1))".

grammar-definition.comment: `.lalrpop` grammar files processed by `build.rs` (`lalrpop::process_src()` / `process_root()`) or the `lalrpop` CLI.

left-recursion.comment: LR generator: the tutorial's canonical precedence tiers are left-recursive (`<l:Expr> "+" <r:Factor>`). Per Assessment Guidelines LR generators get `native`.

ambiguity-handling.comment: Deterministic LR(1)/LALR(1) tables; shift/reduce and reduce/reduce conflicts are reported as errors by the generator (README highlights its conflict error messages).

backtracking.comment: Table-driven LR state machine with state/symbol stacks and single-token lookahead; no backtracking.

lexer-integration.comment: Built-in regex-based lexer (`regex-automata` hybrid DFA, `lexer` feature) generated from the grammar's terminals; or an `extern { enum Tok {...} }` block with any `Iterator<Item = Result<(Loc, Tok, Loc), Error>>`. The book has a dedicated chapter pairing it with `logos`.

precedence-pratt-support.comment: `#[precedence(level="N")]` and `#[assoc(side="left"|"right")]` attributes on alternatives generate the precedence tiers automatically (no yacc-style `%left`/`%right` declarations; the attribute mechanism is the equivalent).

unicode-aware.comment: Built-in lexer works on `&str` and yields `&'input str` slices at byte offsets on char boundaries; the default-on `unicode` feature enables Unicode classes (`\s`, `\d`, ...) in terminal regexes.

input-types.comment: Built-in lexer consumes `&str`. With an `extern` token declaration the parser accepts any iterator of `Result<(Loc, Tok, Loc), E>` (a token slice iterator or a streaming lexer both work). No `&[u8]` support in the built-in lexer.

streaming-partial-input.comment: Tokens are pulled lazily from an iterator, but end-of-iterator is treated as EOF (`UnrecognizedEof`); there is no 'need more input' signal or resumable parser state.

zero-copy.comment: Built-in `Token<'input>` borrows `&'input str`; actions can bind `<&'input str>` into the AST. Custom lexers may likewise yield borrowing tokens ("Using tokens with references" chapter).

span-tracking.comment: `@L`/`@R` bind start/end positions (default `usize` byte offsets). With a custom lexer, `type Location = ...` may be any `Debug + Clone + Default` type (e.g. line/column), so line/col is user-supplied rather than built in.

output-model.comment: Each nonterminal declares its Rust result type; actions construct arbitrary user types (Box<Expr>, i32, ...).

semantic-actions.comment: `=> { rust code }` actions with `<name:Sym>` bindings; `=>?` fallible actions return `Result<T, ParseError>`.

whitespace-comment-handling.comment: Built-in lexer skips whitespace by default; `match { r"\s*" => { }, r"//[^\n\r]*" => { } }` ignore patterns customise skipping (comments etc.). With an external lexer, skipping is the lexer's job.

stateful-parsing.comment: `grammar(scale: i32);` / `grammar<'a>(state: &'a mut S);` declares extra parameters passed to `parse()` and visible in every action (used e.g. for the error-collection Vec).

error-recovery.comment: Per Assessment Guidelines: the `!` error token lets the user decide where recovery is allowed; runtime pops states to one that can shift `!`, drops tokens until the lookahead is accepted, and hands the user an `ErrorRecovery { error, dropped_tokens }`. Parser-level only — lexer errors are not recoverable unless the lexer emits an error token.

multiple-errors-per-parse.comment: Idiom: `grammar<'err>(errors: &'err mut Vec<ErrorRecovery<...>>)` with `! => { errors.push(<>); ... }` collects every recovered error in one run.

expected-token-reporting.comment: `UnrecognizedToken` and `UnrecognizedEof` carry `expected: Vec<String>` (terminal names from the grammar, which docs warn may not be user-presentable as-is).

custom-error-types.comment: `extern { type Error = MyError; }` sets the `E` in `ParseError<L, T, E>`; `map_error`/`map_location`/`map_token` adapt it further.

error-span-fidelity.comment: Guideline 4: `UnrecognizedToken`/`ExtraToken` carry `(L, T, L)` start/end spans and `ErrorRecovery` keeps dropped-token spans; `InvalidToken`/`UnrecognizedEof` carry a single location. No labelled secondary spans.

diagnostic-crate-integration.comment: No first-party or documented bridge to ariadne/miette/codespan-reporting/annotate-snippets; `ParseError` exposes byte spans so users wire up their own reporter (Gluon and Nickel pair it with codespan-reporting).

contextual-error-messages.comment: `!` error-token productions attach rule-specific handling/messages at chosen grammar points; `=>?` actions return `ParseError::User { error }` with custom human-readable errors.

incremental-reparsing.comment: Batch LR parse over a token iterator; no tree reuse or edit API.

lossless-syntax-tree.comment: Whitespace/comments are skipped by the lexer; output is a user-typed AST, not a CST.

syntax-highlighting-queries.comment: No query language or highlighting API.

used-by-lsp-ide.comment: Not used by rust-analyzer, Helix, Zed, or Neovim. Nickel's language server (nls) reuses the LALRPOP-based `nickel-lang-core` parser, but that is a language-specific LSP rather than one of the tagged editors.

runtime-speed-tier.comment: epage/parse-benchmarks-rs JSON benchmark (rustc 1.94.1, lalrpop v0.23.1, checked 2026-09-19): 40 ms parse vs 18 ms for hand-written serde_json (≈2.2×) and 27 ms for winnow → `fast` tier. Maintainer-authored (winnow) but includes all competitors and is reproducible; parsers 'have not been validated'.

compile-time-impact.comment: parse-benchmarks-rs: 12 s debug build for the JSON parser — the slowest in the table (winnow 1 s, pest 3 s). Issue #65 documents a large grammar producing ~1M lines of generated code and 20+ min builds. Generated tables scale with grammar size; keeping `lalrpop` in `[build-dependencies]` only avoids compiling the generator into the final binary.

allocation-strategy.comment: Runtime keeps `Vec` state/symbol stacks (requires `alloc`), so not allocation-free. AST allocation is entirely user-controlled in actions; an arena can be threaded in via grammar parameters.

generated-code-size.comment: parse-benchmarks-rs reports 1,523 KiB release binary overhead for the JSON grammar (vs 67–175 KiB for combinators); issue #65 records ~50 MB of generated source for a PHP expression grammar.

no-std-support.comment: `#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "std"), no_std)]`; `alloc` required (Vec stacks). Since 0.22.0 the built-in lexer is also no_std-compatible. CI runs `cargo hack --feature-powerset` (covers the no-`std` feature set) but has no embedded/`wasm32` target job.

msrv.comment: `rust-version = "1.86"` in workspace Cargo.toml and on crates.io for 0.23.1; CI pins a 1.86 MSRV job. RELEASES.md notes 0.23.0 bumped MSRV to 1.85.

unsafe-usage.comment: No `unsafe` found in lalrpop-util's lib.rs, lexer.rs, or state_machine.rs, but the crate does not declare `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, so tagged minimal rather than forbid. `regex-automata` (dependency) does contain unsafe.

proc-macro-reliance.comment: Code generation happens in `build.rs` (or the CLI); `lalrpop_mod!` is a plain `macro_rules!` include helper. No proc-macro crate in the tree.

build-rs-step.comment: Standard setup: `lalrpop = "0.23"` in `[build-dependencies]` with `lalrpop::process_src()`/`Configuration` in `build.rs`. Alternatively run the `lalrpop` CLI and commit the generated `.rs` to avoid the build script.

dependency-count.comment: Runtime crate `lalrpop-util`: one optional dependency, `regex-automata` (enabled by the default `lexer` feature; zero deps with `default-features = false`). Generator crate `lalrpop` (build-time only) has 13 direct deps.

wasm-compatible.comment: Inferred: runtime is pure Rust, `no_std`-capable, sole dependency `regex-automata`; the generator runs on the host in `build.rs`. No wasm32 CI job or official statement found.

async-friendly.comment: Generated parsers are stateless unit structs; `ParseError`/`ErrorRecovery` are plain enums/Vecs (Send when `L`/`T`/`E` are). Input must be a synchronous token iterator over already-buffered text — no async streaming, but nothing prevents parsing inside an async task.

crates-io-downloads.comment: All-time downloads of the runtime crate `lalrpop-util` as of 2026-09-19 (85.3M); the generator crate `lalrpop` has 69.1M.

maintenance-status.comment: Checked 2026-09-19: commits on 2026-09-14 (clippy, docs) and 2026-07-25 (dep bump); releases 0.23.0 (2026-02) and 0.23.1 (2026-03) within the last 12 months. Original author nikomatsakis is no longer the day-to-day maintainer; dburgener handles most current activity.

documentation-quality.comment: Guideline 4: full book (crash course, 9-chapter tutorial, 6-chapter lexer tutorial, location tracking, cheat sheet) plus docs.rs API docs. No cookbook or formal migration guides beyond RELEASES.md.

tutorial-book.comment: The LALRPOP Book (mdBook) with step-by-step calculator tutorial and lexer tutorial.

notable-users.value: Gluon (parser crate), Nickel (nickel-lang-core), Solang Solidity compiler (solang-parser)
notable-users.comment: All three verified via `lalrpop-util` dependency + `lalrpop` build-dependency in their Cargo.toml (checked 2026-09-19). The README still lists RustPython, but RustPython's current workspace uses `ruff_python_parser` and no longer depends on lalrpop.

bus-factor.comment: lalrpop GitHub org; crate owners Niko Matsakis, Daniel Burgener (dburgener) and the org team. History: nikomatsakis 743, Marwes 245, dburgener 113, Pat-Lafon 73, youknowone 64 commits; recent activity is mostly dburgener plus occasional contributors.
